TITHE REGULATOR, THIRD FURNACE. Draw to the Gaol's restraints: constant, by day and by night, whatever the yield.
Stock is renewed by the quarter's census. Any shortfall in yield is to be made good from the March. Do not open the governor while the furnace is drawing.

Doc(\"The Covenant of Ascent (cut under.t: The Covenant of Ascent (cut under the throne)
s: The Covenant of Ascent (cut under the throne) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
Let the King's person stand for his dominion, his continuance for its elevation, and his census for the extent of his assent.
Let tribute renew what fear first purchased. Let no departure of the creditor release the signatory from the instrument he continues to bear.

Doc(\"Notes from a failed wyvern capture.t: Notes from a failed wyvern capture (the Needles)
s: Notes from a failed wyvern capture (the Needles) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
Nets taught it to avoid us. Meat brought the smaller ones. The great animal used the upper arch each morning before the wind changed.
Pell saw a way down to its back and would not attempt it. I called him a coward. After what happened to the tower, I owe him a better word.
Last entry, another hand: Expedition withdrawn by order. The high animal is not to be pursued further. The Crown has no need of a way up that it does not already control.

Doc(\"Vaelis on the passage spell (at th.t: Vaelis on the passage spell (at the ward bench)
s: Vaelis on the passage spell (at the ward bench) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

I cannot make us stronger than the ward. I can make the ward answer a different question. The seal says the inspection may enter. My work is to ensure that, for the length of our passage, it sees the inspection when it sees us.
The creature must be included. Forget its signature and we arrive without it.

Doc(\"The Preserver and His People (a Cr.t: The Preserver and His People (a Crownreach schoolbook)
s: The Preserver and His People (a Crownreach schoolbook) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

When the lower world could no longer sustain human life, His Majesty gathered all who could be saved. The City rose by the strength of his devotion. Those who remained below are remembered in our morning prayer. Let no child mistake the shapes seen on clear days for inhabited towns. Ruin often resembles a home at a distance.

On the same desk, the schoolroom's supply ledger, in a clerk's hand: Flour, fine, forty sacks - Fenn Ford. Flour, coarse, sixty - Three Toll. Barley, twenty - Briar's Rest. Received by the Long Kitchen against the quarter's allowance.
The landing register (the Landing Registry) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

Permissions to descend: none granted this year. None granted last year. A note against the column, in red: Hereditary landing rights lapsed with the Fennick line; to be reissued at His Majesty's pleasure.
Permissions to ascend: Royal service, by collection, as required. Chancellor's office. No petition accepted.
At the foot of the page, in a different hand, very small: 'Nobody goes down. Then why do we keep the barges oiled?'

Doc(\"Bonds of service, House Merrow (th.t: Bonds of service, House Merrow (the Landing Registry)
s: Bonds of service, House Merrow (the Landing Registry) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

Bond of the Ashcombe family, four persons: in service to House Merrow until the debt of passage is discharged. Debt of passage incurred: Year 0. Interest: to be added annually. Present balance: greater than at issue.
Bond of the Tull family, three persons: as above. Bond of the Pryor family: as above. Each signed with a mark. Each marked, below, 'not to leave the House without the House's leave'.
They are not the prisoners of the Last Gaol. But they have been paying for the same journey for two hundred and eighty-seven years.
Sealed calculation by Corvin Hale is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

Every measurement follows the King's condition. The foundations do not possess an independent reserve sufficient for sustained elevation. A local ward may delay a fracture. No local ward can hold the whole. If his life ends, descent begins.
I have recopied this three times because I fear what I will do if only one copy exists.
A letter carried down is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

If there are trees where we land, please ask whether I may climb one. We have trees here, but the gardeners say the roots belong to the foundations and we must not touch them. I have packed my school map. Mother says we may need a different map now.

Doc(\"A letter for Edda (from Mara's bun.t: A letter for Edda (from Mara's bundle)
s: A letter for Edda (from Mara's bundle) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
To Edda Venn, taken for service in the year of the long frost, if anybody ever goes up.

The bees came through the winter. Father is the same. I have named my girl after you, so there is an Edda in the house again, and when she shouts it is like having you back. I do not know if they let you read up there. I am writing anyway. Somebody should be writing to you.
Folded inside, in Mara's hand: 'My grandmother's sister. Nobody ever went up. Take it anyway.'

Doc(\"A notice on a door (the outer stre.t: A notice on a door (the outer street)
s: A notice on a door (the outer street) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
BY ORDER OF THE CROWN. THE KING'S PEACE.

The streets of the outer city are closed until further notice. Households will remain within doors. Any household found to have sheltered persons from below, or to have assisted in the unlawful descent from the service quarter, will be entered in the register for the next collection.
Long live the King, who preserves us.
Under it someone has chalked, very small, the number of their household, and crossed it out, and chalked it again.
The Processional of Kings (the plinths) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
ALDREN II, THE STEADFAST. YEAR 41 TO YEAR 79. HE KEPT THE CITY WHOLE.
ALDREN VI, THE MERCIFUL. YEAR 171 TO YEAR 203.

Eight kings and one face: the long nose, the heavy brow, the same set of the mouth, cut by the same workshop - the same mason's mark is on every plinth. The ninth plinth's second date has never been cut. The stone of the ninth is the oldest of the eight.
Under it, scratched very small, at knee height, where a child would scratch: SAME NOSE.

Doc(\"The Long Gallery (a card in a fram.t: The Long Gallery (a card in a frame)
s: The Long Gallery (a card in a frame) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
Portraits of His Majesty, kept privately. Not to be copied.

Year 1, by Tolland: the King in his thirty-eighth year. Year 31, by Hesk. Year 64, by Hesk's daughter. Year 102, unsigned. Year 140, by Ordway. Year 171, by Ordway's pupil. Year 203, by Lisle. Year 238, by Lisle's grandson. Year 266, by Maren Doyle. Year 280, by Maren Doyle, Court Painter, who was told to paint him younger and did not.

One man, ten times. The hair goes from dark to white so slowly you have to walk back up the gallery to be sure it has. In the last one he is looking at the painter as if she has said something he will remember.
At the end of the gallery, a small panel by Tolland: the Queen and the Princess, the year before the Ascent. The varnish on it has been renewed many more times than on any of the others.

Doc(\"A letter, the year before the Asce.t: A letter, the year before the Ascent
s: A letter, the year before the Ascent is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

The physicians say the fever has reached Tanners' Row, and the ward at the north gate is failing faster than Vaelis can mend it. I have signed the levies. I have signed the quarantine of the river wards. I will sign whatever keeps the gate shut between the fever and this house.
Ise asked me tonight whether the city would still be here when she is grown. I told her it would.
Write back and tell me I did not lie to her.
Private notes of the King is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
In the margins of an early account of the evacuation of the capital, in a much later hand:

They write as though I chose between a whole kingdom and a broken one. There was no whole kingdom left to choose. Yet every year they ask me to choose again. I have built a city in which children live long enough to accuse me. Below, they teach theirs to do the same.
The year's tribute, annotated is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).
Year 211. Quota by district, with the King's hand in the margin.

Fenn Ford: fourteen. (May bear eleven more: their harvest was good.) Reedwake: nine. (No more: they are the only boats on the Wend.) Hallow Weir: six. Three Toll: twelve. (The road needs them alive. Take from the outlying farms.) Briar's Rest: four. (A waystation. Leave the smith.)
At the foot of the page, in the same hand, smaller: 'Every number is a name below. I stopped reading the names in the eighties. I still sign.'

Doc(\"The empty sky (the Briar's Rest re.t: The empty sky (the Briar's Rest record)
s: The empty sky (the Briar's Rest record) is one of the papers of the story. Read it where you find it (E) and it's kept in your journal (L).

At dawn we could see the ridge without the city above it. We counted forty-three arrivals before breakfast and more after. Mara says to count blankets instead of people for the next hour. Oren has taken the royal sign off the gate. Nobody stopped him.

Clear is a kind of weather. Clear skies: the sun, the stars, and nothing in the way.
Overcast is a kind of weather. Grey cloud over everything; the light is flat and the nights are darker.
Drizzle is a kind of weather. A thin rain. Not much, but it puts out small fires.
Rain is a kind of weather. Steady rain. Fires gutter, the ground darkens, sound carries less.
Storm is a kind of weather. Thunder and heavy rain. Lightning strikes the high ground (Storm damage) - don't stand on a hilltop holding iron.
Monsoon is a kind of weather. Rain like a wall. Rivers rise and low ground floods.
Hurricane is a kind of weather. A storm with wind enough to throw you; lightning, floods and wreckage.
Tornado is a kind of weather. A funnel that walks the land and lifts whatever it reaches.
Snow is a kind of weather. Snow falls and settles. It's cold.
Blizzard is a kind of weather. Driving snow, wind and bitter cold: you can't see far and you'll freeze without fur.
Hail is a kind of weather. Ice from the sky: every stone that hits you hurts (Frost damage). Get under cover.
Fog is a kind of weather. Thick fog: you see little and so does everything else.
Sand is a kind of weather. A sandstorm: wind and grit, and the sun gone brown.
Ash is a kind of weather. Ash falls from a burning sky; the air is hot and grey.
Embers is a kind of weather. Glowing embers drift on a hot wind.
Spores is a kind of weather. Fungal spores hang in the air, glowing faintly.
Petals is a kind of weather. Petals on the wind.
Motes is a kind of weather. Motes of strange light drift down.

Rootways is a kind of cave: where the old trees drink. Caves open under the land everywhere, shallow near the surface and stranger the deeper you go (below about 28 m, and again below 58 m).

Weeping Caverns is a kind of cave: the drip of ten thousand years. Caves open under the land everywhere, shallow near the surface and stranger the deeper you go (below about 28 m, and again below 58 m).
Spider Nest is a kind of cave: something is watching. Caves open under the land everywhere, shallow near the surface and stranger the deeper you go (below about 28 m, and again below 58 m).
Salt Caverns is a kind of cave: white halls of the dead sea. Caves open under the land everywhere, shallow near the surface and stranger the deeper you go (below about 28 m, and again below 58 m).

Fungal Depths is a kind of cave: the forest that never saw the sun. Caves open under the land everywhere, shallow near the surface and stranger the deeper you go (below about 28 m, and again below 58 m).

Reed Shallows - the lake's edge, thick with reeds. The shallow margin of a lake: reeds stand out of the water, lily pads float over a carpet of stonewort, and minnows and sticklebacks dart through the weed in their hundreds.
Lily Garden - under a roof of lily pads. A warm, still lake roofed with lily pads and lotus, the light coming down green between them onto soft weed. Koi and carp drift beneath.
Pondweed Meadow - a meadow of weed, swaying. Open water over a lake bed grown thick with pondweed and stonewort, swaying like a field in the wind. Perch and roach shoal through it; pike wait in it.

Drowned Grove - a wood the lake rose over. Where a lake rose over a wood: dead trunks stand up out of the water, fallen logs and stumps lie furred with weed, and roots arch over the silt. Trout and bass hide among them, and eels at night.

Glacial Tarn - cold, and clear to the bottom. A cold mountain or northern lake, clear as glass and turquoise with rock flour: a floor of grey pebbles and boulders, a little stonewort, and char, trout and grayling hanging in the cold.

Blackwater Bog - the water dark as tea. A bog lake stained dark as tea with peat: drowned roots and sunken logs in a soft black floor, tangled weed, and old fish of the murk - bowfin, gar, catfish, snakehead and eels.

Flooded Jungle - the forest under the flood. A warm brown lake through a drowned jungle, roots and fallen trunks everywhere, giant lilies overhead. Shoals of neon tetras and discus, piranha in packs, and the great arapaima rising to breathe.

Crystal Spring - a spring, white sand and clear water. A spring-fed pool over white sand and pebbles, so clear the fish seem to hang in air. Trout, sticklebacks and minnows; pupfish where the land is hot.

Mussel Shoals - a lake bed paved with mussels. Rocky lake bed paved with beds of mussels between the boulders, sponges on the stones. Walleye and perch hunt over them, and now and then an old sturgeon noses through.

Lake Deeps - the dark middle of the lake. The cold dark middle of a deep lake: silt, a few rocks and fallen logs, now and then something that sank - a pot, an anchor, a boat. Sturgeon, paddlefish, burbot and catfish keep to the bottom.

Salt Lake - brine, and stone that grew. A salt or desert lake: stromatolites - stone built up by slime over ages - stand in the shallows, the floor crusted white and carpeted with coloured mats of living slime. Pupfish and tilapia, little else.

Hot Spring Lake - warm water over the fire below. A lake warmed from below: vents breathe sulphur through a floor of orange, yellow and green mats of living slime that grow only in the heat. Tilapia and pupfish bear it.

Bone Mere - something drowned here, many times. A lake in the grim lands, black and still: bones lie on its floor among sunken trunks and roots, and pale weed glows faintly over them. Eels, catfish and piranha feed here and do not go hungry.

Coral Garden - the reef, alive in every colour. A warm, shallow reef of branching, fan, brain and table corals, anemones, sponges and giant clams, every hollow full of fish: clownfish, tangs, angelfish, parrotfish, butterflyfish, triggerfish, lionfish, and reef sharks, turtles and octopus among them.

Seagrass Meadow - a meadow under the sea. Shallow sand grown over with seagrass as thick as a hayfield, starfish and sand dollars between the blades. Turtles, manatees and dugongs graze it; rays and cuttlefish hunt it.

Kelp Forest - a forest of kelp, to the light. Cool sea where giant kelp grows from the rocks to the surface in tall swaying columns, urchins and anemones below. Garibaldi, rockfish, cod and salmon, octopus and lobster in the rocks.

Rocky Reef - rock, and everything that clings to it. A shelf of rock and boulders crusted with mussels, urchins, anemones and sponges, starfish in every crack. Rockfish, wolf eels, cod, octopus and lobster.

Glass Sponge Reef - a reef of glass, in the cold. Deep cold water where glass sponges have built reefs over thousands of years, pale vases and chimneys of silica, sea pens and soft corals among them. Rockfish and halibut; spider crabs and squid.

Wreck Graveyard - where the ships went down. A stretch of sea floor where ships have gone down for as long as there have been ships: hulls, anchors, spilled amphorae, timbers, all grown over with mussels and anemones. Groupers, barracuda, morays and nurse sharks keep house in them.

Sunken Ruins - a city the sea took. The ruins of a place the sea took: columns and walls and great stone heads lie half-buried in sand and seagrass, coral growing on them, amphorae spilled in the streets. Groupers, octopus and reef fish live in the houses now.

Midnight Abyss - where the light never reaches. The deep sea floor beyond the light: black silt flecked with things that glow, glowing sea pens, glass sponges, the bones of whales that fell. Anglerfish, viperfish, lanternfish, gulper eels, vampire squid, and the giant squid.

Hydrothermal Vents - black smoke, and life without the sun. Chimneys of black rock pouring hot water up from under the sea floor, crowded round with tube worms, vent mussels and white mats of slime that live on the heat and sulphur alone. Yeti crabs and eelpouts.

Polar Shelf - under the ice-cold sea. The cold shelf of the polar seas: soft corals, glass sponges, urchins and anemones on grey stone and ice-dropped boulders. Polar cod in shoals, icefish with clear blood, belugas and narwhals overhead.

Mangrove Roots - among the roots, where sea meets land. Warm shallows where the sea runs in among arching roots, oysters crusting them and seagrass between. A nursery: snappers, archerfish, mudskippers, and the odd bull shark come up with the tide.

Patch Reef Lagoon - white sand, and heads of coral in it. The sheltered water behind a reef: bright sand and seagrass, and standing up out of it here and there a round head of coral - a bommie - crowded with fish. Rays rest in the sand between.

Reef Wall - the reef's edge, straight down into the blue. Where the reef ends in a wall dropping hundreds of metres into blue water: fans and sponges grow out from it into the current, the biggest at the top, black coral and whips further down. Sharks, jacks and turtles patrol its face.

Bathyal Mud - the slope, in the last of the light. The continental slope, going down into the dark: soft olive mud worked over by everything living in it - mounds and burrows and trails - sea pens and brittle stars on it, sea cucumbers ploughing it. Grenadiers, ratfish, sablefish and hagfish.

Cold-water Coral Mound - a reef in the dark and the cold. Coral without sunlight: thickets of white and salmon-pink stony coral built up over thousands of years into mounds on the slope, their dead branches rubble all round, bamboo and black coral and red fans among them. Orange roughy and squat lobsters by the thousand.

Canyon Walls - down the canyon, layer under layer. A canyon cut down through the slope, its walls the sea floor's own layers laid bare, ledges of mud and fallen rock, corals and sponges hanging out over the drop. Sixgill sharks come up it at night.

Abyssal Ooze - the abyssal plain, in the dark. The floor of the open ocean, a kilometre and more down: red-brown clay that settles a millimetre in a thousand years, strewn with black manganese nodules, giant single-celled xenophyophores, and sea cucumbers walking it on their tube feet. Tripod fish stand on their fins facing into the current.

Hadal Floor - the bottom of the trench. The floor of a trench, three and four kilometres down and more: pale ooze, rock fallen from the walls, and life that wants no light at all - snailfish, the deepest fish there are, pale and soft as jelly; swarms of amphipods; sea cucumbers; giant isopods. The cold is near freezing and the weight of water above is past imagining.

Brine Pool - a lake at the bottom of the sea. Where gas and brine seep up out of the slope: pools of brine so heavy they lie on the sea floor like lakes, with a surface and a shore, ringed thick with mussels that live on the methane, white mats of bacteria, tube worms. Anything that swims into the brine dies of it.

Whale Fall - where a whale came to rest. A whale that died and sank: for decades its bones feed a whole world in the dark - hagfish and sleeper sharks on the flesh, then worms and crabs in their thousands, then bacteria in the bones themselves, white mats spreading out from them.

Blue Hole - a hole in the sea, going down into the dark. A sinkhole in the shallows, a cave whose roof fell in when the sea was lower: the bright sand ends in a ring of coral and the water goes from turquoise to ink-blue straight down. Its walls are bare white limestone; far down the water turns still and lifeless.

Seamount Garden - a mountain under the sea. The flanks of a seamount, standing up out of the deep into the currents: gardens of bamboo coral, black coral, red fans and sponges on its rock, and fish gathered round it from all the empty ocean - orange roughy in their shoals, hammerheads above.

Spoilers: a place of the story.
Saint Orra's Isle is a place of the story. An island out in the strait, once a sanctuary, now the inspector's prison, with its guards, cells, barracks and the inspection chamber far below.
Spoilers: a place of the story.
The Needles is a place of the story. Spires of rock on a broad shoulder high on Mount Hessaril, above the cloud, where the high wyvern hunts; the Crown's old capture camp at their foot.
Spoilers: a place of the story.

Mount Hessaril is a place of the story. The Worldspine's mountain east of Briar's Rest: four kilometres and more of rock and ice, ten times the height of any other peak. Storm drakes roost at its foot; wild high wyverns circle its summit.

comes straight on, hits hard, slow to recover
measured: blocks, steps back, counters after a dodge
follows unseen, waits for an opening
lies still until you're close, then pounces
hunts with its kin: the alpha engages, the rest flank
warns you off; fights only if you push in, and won't follow far
Some creatures have a quirk: a trick of their own that they teach you the hard way.
It burst into more of itself. Smaller - but there are more of them now.
Something is moving under the ground toward you. When the earth heaves, get off that spot.
Its shell turned your blow. Get round behind it.
It snatched something from your pack and ran! Bring it down before it's gone.
Its young pour out of it!
Its kin saw that. They're coming for you, mad with it.
It's latched onto you, drinking. Jump twice or roll to throw it off.
It was on you before you saw it. Watch for the shimmer in the air.
It fed on what it killed, and grew.
It called out - and something answered.
It isn't where you struck. Look behind you.
It threw you. Up here, keep the mountain at your back and the drop in front of it.
They were under the snow all round you.
The keys, and what they do. Every one of these can be changed in Settings.
WASD move. Space jumps (and climbs: run at a ledge and you grab it and pull yourself up). Shift sprints; tap it to roll out of a blow. Ctrl crouches (quieter, harder to see).

Left mouse attacks, harvests and casts; hold it to charge a heavy blow or draw a bow. Right mouse uses what's in your hand: eat, drink, place, equip. E interacts and picks things up. Q drops. 1-9 or the wheel choose a hotbar slot. R switches a staff's spell.
Tab inventory and crafting. J bestiary. M map. L journal. V or F5 third person. F1 this wiki (over something in a menu: its page). F11 full screen. / the console. Escape pause.
The story's soldiers, guards, workers and crowds stand at their posts from the first day. Kill them before the story gets there and they stay dead - the story doesn't count it.
The music: a day piece and a night piece for every land, others for caves, dungeons, bosses of every kind, combat, the war, the title and death. It changes with where you are and what's happening.
You can build: hold a block material and right-click a surface. Pieces snap to a grid, need support from below or beside, and come in many materials and paints.
The people of the world belong to factions, and the factions feud.
villagers, farmers, merchants, town guards: peaceful unless you hurt one of them - then the guards come and the rest run
the bandits, the cult and the undead
hunters, mercenaries, monks, druids, priests: keep to themselves
brigands, thugs, barbarians, assassins, gladiators, warlords: hostile
soldiers, bowmen, knights and executioners garrisoning the old castles
bandits, the cult, the undead and the rogue mages
pyromancers, cryomancers, stormcallers, warlocks of the towers

Somewhere in the world two armies besiege a castle, night and day: hundreds of soldiers in formation, knights, archers loosing volleys, catapults and siege engines. You can watch it from the hills or walk into the melee.
carries soldiers up to the walls
Console: /war (above the field), /war front (beside the line), /war melee (in the fight).
When something kills you, it remembers. It takes a name and an epithet for what it did, grows stronger, and turns up again - up to five of them at once. Kill your nemesis and its name is struck off.
The creature or brigand that brings you down takes a name of its own and the name of what it did to you - Grisk Ironjaw, Morwen the Widowmaker - and grows on it: stronger, harder, a new trick or two.
Some while later, wherever you are under the open sky, it comes looking for you.
Kill you again and it grows again. Wound it badly and it may slip away to lick its wounds, and come back scarred and angrier.
Bring it down for good and it leaves you a trophy, and something worth having from whatever it had hoarded.
At most five hunt you at once (an old one is forgotten for a new one); they're kept with your world.

Feed a tameable creature what it eats and it may follow you (up to three companions at once). Passive, skittish and neutral creatures can be tamed, and wolves and cats of any kind, and some of the wild things (dire wolves, ironshells, hollow stags, lantern wisps, thornbacks, glass scuttlers). People, bosses, horrors, demons, swimmers and anything very large can't.

The storm drake roosts at the foot of Mount Hessaril: feed it meat three times and ride it up the mountain's wind as far as the Needles. The high wyvern hunts over the Needles: drop onto its back from the overhanging ledge and ride out its bucking. Q loops, F barrel-rolls, X whistles; it tires the higher it climbs.

The Vestibule is the way into the bowl, before the first circle of the Inferno, where the Uncommitted are.
"Those who lived without disgrace and without praise, chasing a blank banner forever."
Stand still here and the wasps find you. Cross the Acheron to the way down.

i: The Unbaptized and the Virtuous Pagans
s: Limbo is the first circle of the Inferno, where the Unbaptized and the Virtuous Pagans are.
"No weeping here, only sighs that make the eternal air tremble."
Without hope: your wounds won't close, but in the light of the noble castle.
The Circle of Lust is the second circle of the Inferno, where the Lustful are.
"The infernal hurricane that never rests hurtles the spirits in its rapine."
The storm throws you about, and the Night Hags' song draws you to them.
The Circle of Gluttony is the third circle of the Inferno, where the Gluttonous are.
"Rain eternal, cursed, cold and heavy; hail and filthy water and snow through the dark."
Hunger gnaws three times as fast. The larders feed you - when the food isn't rotten.
The Circle of Greed is the fourth circle of the Inferno, where the Hoarders and the Wasters are.
"Rolling weights by force of chest, they crash together, crying 'Why hoard?' and 'Why waste?'."
Chests everywhere: riches, or a mimic that kills in a bite, or gold too heavy to carry.
The Circle of Wrath is the fifth circle of the Inferno, where the Wrathful and the Sullen are.
"In the black marsh of Styx they strike each other; under it the sullen gurgle in the mud."
Everything here is berserk. The sullen in the pools drag at you. Dis guards the way down.
The City of Dis is the sixth circle of the Inferno, where the Heretics are.
"Among the tombs the flames were scattered, so that they glowed more than iron in the forge."
The open tombs burn. The sealed ones hold relics - and whatever was buried with them.
The Circle of Violence is the seventh circle of the Inferno, where the Violent are.
"A river of blood boils those who did harm by force; past it a wood, past that a burning sand."
Blood calls for blood: every life you take here calls up another to avenge it.
Malebolge is the eighth circle of the Inferno, where the Fraudulent are.
"Ten evil ditches cut in stone the colour of iron, and bridges of rock running across them."
Trust nothing: not every bridge is there, and half the chests are mouths.
Cocytus is the ninth circle of the Inferno, where the Traitors are.
"A lake so frozen it looked like glass, not water; the traitors in it to the face, their tears turned to ice."
What you tamed turns on you. Stand still and the ice takes you. Past Lucifer, the way out.
